items.stem: A company wants to extend SAP ERP without changing the core so upgrades stay clean. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Modify the ERP source code directly
options.rationale: Core modification complicates upgrades, the exact outcome to avoid.

options.text: Build a side-by-side extension on the platform
options.rationale: Correct: side-by-side extensibility keeps custom logic off the core, preserving clean upgrades.
Spreadsheets do not extend the ERP functionally.
Disabling modules removes needed functionality and is not an extension approach.

items.explanation: Correct: side-by-side extensibility keeps custom logic off the core, preserving clean upgrades.

items.stem: Within the platform account model, what is the typical relationship between a global account and a subaccount?

options.text: A subaccount contains many global accounts
options.rationale: The hierarchy is the reverse of this.

options.text: A global account can contain multiple subaccounts
options.rationale: Correct: a global account is the top-level contract entity holding one or more subaccounts.
They are part of one hierarchical account model.

options.text: A global account is a single application
options.rationale: A global account is an organisational/contract construct, not an app.

items.explanation: Correct: a global account is the top-level contract entity holding one or more subaccounts.

options.text: Authentication via a trusted identity provider
options.rationale: Correct: establishing trust with an IdP is an authentication concept.

Packaging design is irrelevant to platform administration.
